daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

DPR Deputy Speaker Dasco Azhar announced that political safaris on electoral law revision will begin during the upcoming DPR recess period. The National Legislation Body (Banggar) also confirmed that the 2027 budget for the Free Nutritious Meals (MBG) program has been set at Rp 174 trillion. Meanwhile, an Education Ministry official explained that the MBG program will eventually target only students in need, with the role of school canteens still under review.

  • The National Party of Awakening (PKB) invited President Prabowo to its 28th anniversary celebration.
  • PDIP official Said responded to PSI's ambitions to make Central Java its stronghold.
  • An anggota DPR criticized Forestry Minister Raja Juli over his handling of a gratuity report from the Regent of Kuansing, which KPK later confirmed was only reported on the previous Friday.
  • An anggota DPR called for the Cyber Security Bill to be passed swiftly, citing increasingly tangible threats.
  • Commission IV of the DPR formed a special team to investigate mining waste in Mimika, a problem dating back to 1967.
  • The Ministry of Home Affairs coordinated regional proposals for the BSPS housing subsidy program.
  • The Head of the Budget Committee (Banggar) rejected a proposal to raise regional head salaries.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo Subianto and Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong held a Leaders' Retreat that yielded 26 bilateral agreements. The two leaders reaffirmed the Malacca Strait remains open under UNCLOS and pledged to uphold ASEAN's stance on peaceful dispute resolution. PM Wong stated that Singapore believes in Indonesia's future, while Prabowo said any misunderstandings will be resolved as friends.

  • Indonesia's Foreign Minister and MPR Speaker will attend the funeral of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in Iran.
  • President Prabowo assigned Danantara to implement a power export agreement with Singapore.
  • Singapore is pushing for more direct flights to Indonesia.
  • An Indonesian woman was stabbed to death in an apartment in Japan.

Other

Indonesian police announced charges in a major corruption case linked to the blackout crisis, stating that coal corruption triggered the blackout and caused state losses of Rp 5 trillion. Police revealed the modus operandi involved manipulation of quality and contract prices for coal supplied to power plants. Investigators said they will soon examine the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources in connection with the case.

  • Investment in Indonesia's Special Economic Zones (SEZ) reached Rp 353.5 trillion and created 266,000 jobs.
  • The Minister of Manpower addressed a proposal to include high school and vocational graduates in the National Internship program.
  • The Health Ministry temporarily suspended anesthesiology education at Kandou Hospital following the death of a specialist trainee doctor.
  • Indonesia's carbon trading value is expected to reach Rp 5 trillion.
  • BPOM warned that microplastics may increase stroke risk.
